speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Sarcoidosis (specifically Lupus Pernio variant or Sarcoid Ulcer)

Based on your history of Crohn's disease, the one-month duration, and the progression from a red spot to an ulcer following a minor trauma (ant bite), I suspect a granulomatous reaction. Your history of uveitis and steroid use also raises concern for sarcoidosis. I would like to confirm this with a skin biopsy and check your chest for involvement.
